summary: CAL FIRE lookout in Lassen County built 1966 from a redesigned BC-3 cab; staffed intermittently during predicted lightning events as of 2015; still on CAL FIRE's 2022 list.

facts.design: Re-design of the BC-3 cab, with a 64 sq ft reduced-scale prototype tested first; the 38-foot three-legged steel tower came from Thompson Peak, Plumas National Forest
facts.agency: California Department of Forestry and Fire Protection, Lassen-Modoc Unit (Cal Fire LMU)

access.note: No source read describes public access; CAL FIRE says it does not rent its lookouts (2008 fact sheet)

notes_for_editor: Brief record matches the Register (built 1966, NHLR registered 2019). Staffing 'seasonal' is an approximation of 'intermittently during predicted lightning events'. The 2008 CAL FIRE table places a 'Destroyed during the Rumsey Fire in 2004' note beside Berryessa Peak (Napa County), not Likely Mountain; do not read it as a loss for this lookout. No source read describes the lookout's condition, public access, or any fire it spotted. The Forest Lookouts page for Likely Mountain has no history text, only a county list. Brief elevation_m 2248.5 vs Register 2,249 m is consistent. Fact-check 2026-10-08: the story no longer says staffing has been occasional; the Register dates intermittent staffing only to 2015.
